newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed lower on Wednesday after some choppy trading influenced by blips in the U.S. and German markets, dealers said.
Guilders slipped early along with other Euros after the U.S. market had pulled back overnight on concerns about the validity of an earlier encouraging employment costs number.
The domestic market turned choppy after U.S. December durable goods orders were released in the afternoon, with bunds and Treasuries blipping up and then sinking back again.
Volume remained moderate with trading more dealer-driven than investor-driven, one broker said.
"Everyone is a little bit nervous and investors are starting to hesitate about buying the long end and starting to look to move into the middle," he said.
There was also bid interest in the short end, traders said, with 1999 to 2001 paper in demand.
The mood in the market was cautious, they said, though not overly negative.
"We haven't yet built up a really pessimistic feeling, things are just volatile at the moment," one said.
Spreads to Germany moved in slightly, but dealers said Guilders could still outperform in the near term.

A one billion guilder European Investment Bank guilder-into-euro issue during the afternoon had not attracted much attention, one broker said. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
